title: Pool round trip: ADBC fetch_record_batch → DuckDB 2.0 → Arrow → psycopg Copy.set_types or pgpq
question: Do absent versus null inside JSONB, JSON text, NUMERIC exactness and timestamptz instants survive ADBC 1.13 fetch_record_batch → DuckDB 2.0 relation (one join, one group-by) → Arrow → PostgreSQL by psycopg Copy.set_types and by pgpq 0.12; how does the loader bind the run and cut given ADBC's parameter limits; what memory does one join hold?
method: Database p0q_pool cloned from cs_template on 18/corpus (dropped afterwards). Nine hand-made rows covering JSONB present-null/absent/false/JSON-null/SQL-NULL, big and tiny JSON numbers, unicode, a json column with whitespace, order and duplicate keys, NUMERIC with 39 digits, 1.50, 1e-40, NaN and ±Infinity, timestamptz at year 1, both epochs, 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999 and odd offsets, plus a dimension table. ADBC fetch_record_batch → read_all → DuckDB register, join USING (kind) and group-by with json_exists and ->, rel.to_arrow_table() → (a) psycopg binary COPY with Copy.set_types (Jsonb/Json with identity dumps, Decimal) and (b) pgpq new_with_encoders with the JSONB string encoder → Copy.write, NUMERIC as text, as decimal128(38, 9) and through a text staging table; 11 SQL checks per row against the source. Also psycopg as loader, ±infinity, $1 SELECT binding and the temp-table route with statements read from pg_stat_statements, DuckDB 2.0 result lifecycle, and memory at 10^5 and 10^6 observations (~290 B JSONB) joined with 2x10^4 claims (VmRSS, pa.total_allocated_bytes, DuckDB JSON-profiling system.peak_buffer_memory). Versions: adbc-driver-postgresql 1.13.0, duckdb 2.0.0, pyarrow 26.0.0, pgpq 0.12.0, psycopg 3.3.6, PostgreSQL 18.6; same machine as p0q.fk-cost.

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/q4_*, code/q5_*, code/q4_s6/, results/q4/, results/q5/, records/p0q.fk-cost.json, records/p0q.pool-roundtrip.json and the README's Q-4 and Q-5 sections

conclusion: Absent versus null, JSON text, NUMERIC exactness and timestamptz instants survive ADBC → DuckDB 2.0 → psycopg Copy.set_types on every case (given identity dumps for JSON text, Decimal for NUMERIC and a UTC cast before to_pylist), and survive pgpq only with NUMERIC through a text staging table and a server-side cast (text is refused by the server, decimal128 by Arrow); ±infinity timestamps do not survive ADBC. ADBC returns NUMERIC as arrow.opaque strings, accepts $1 SELECTs in 1.13 but then leaves the COPY transport (about 1.4x slower), and loads 2.1x faster than psycopg at 10^6 rows with a third of the memory; one join holds about 20 MB of DuckDB buffer, with the output Arrow as a full copy. Inputs: P0-P-1 loads with ADBC, binding the run and cut as literals or via a temporary table, NUMERIC kept as text, DuckDB TimeZone pinned to UTC, one open result per connection; P0-P-3 stays on psycopg Copy.set_types and does not adopt pgpq unless a measured writer cost calls for it (then with the staging step).
